title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Download UCI files into REPRO_DATA_CACHE (shared cache), with echo of shapes."""
import os
import sys
import urllib.request

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(".cache", "datasets", "files")
os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)

URLS = {
    "hepatitis.data": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
}


def fetch(name, url):
    dest = os.path.join(CACHE, name)
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0:
        print(f"[cache hit] {name} -> {dest}")
        return dest
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (repro)"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        data = r.read()
    with open(dest, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    print(f"[downloaded] {name} {len(data)} bytes -> {dest}")
    return dest


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for name, url in URLS.items():
        try:
            p = fetch(name, url)
            with open(p, "r", errors="replace") as f:
                lines = [ln.rstrip("\n") for ln in f if ln.strip()]
            print(f"{name}: {len(lines)} non-empty lines; first line:")
            print(" ", lines[0][:200])
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"FAILED {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            sys.exit(1)

"""Dataset loading for the proximity-kernel reproduction.

Target claim C1: UCI Hepatitis (Table 2 row "Hepatitis": 155 samples, 19
features, 13 categorical + 6 numeric, 5.67% missing values, 2 classes).

All UCI files are cached in REPRO_DATA_CACHE (shared across runs); if absent
they are downloaded from archive.ics.uci.edu.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import urllib.request

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

MISSING_MARKERS = ["?", "", "NaN", "nan", "NA", "N/A", "null", "None"]


def cache_dir() -> str:
    return os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(
        ".cache", "datasets", "files"
    )


# Registry: UCI files used by the paper. Table 2 statistics are asserted after
# loading so a wrong file is caught immediately.
DATASETS = {
    "hepatitis": {
        "filename": "hepatitis.data",
        "url": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
        "n_samples": 155,
        "n_features": 19,
        "n_classes": 2,
        # Column 0 is the class: 1 = DIE, 2 = LIVE (UCI documentation).
        "class_map": {1: 0, 2: 1},
        "target_col": 0,
        "note": "UCI 'Hepatitis' domain; raw numeric codes kept for both the "
        "13 categorical (SEX, STEROID, ANTIVIRALS, FATIGUE, MALAISE, ANOREXIA, "
        "LIVER_BIG, LIVER_FIRM, SPLEEN_PALPABLE, SPIDERS, ASCITES, VARICES, "
        "HISTOLOGY) and 6 numeric features (assumption A1: categorical values "
        "are ordinal codes treated as numeric).",
    },
}


def _fetch(name: str, url: str) -> str:
    """Return a cached local path for `url`, downloading it if necessary."""
    dest = os.path.join(cache_dir(), name)
    if os.path.exists(dest) and os.path.getsize(dest) > 0:
        return dest
    os.makedirs(cache_dir(), exist_ok=True)
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (repro)"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        data = r.read()
    tmp = dest + ".part"
    with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    os.replace(tmp, dest)
    return dest


def load_dataset(name: str = "hepatitis") -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, dict]:
    """Load a dataset as (X, y, meta).

    X: float array (n_samples, n_features) with NaN for missing values.
    y: int array (n_samples,) with class labels coded 0..n_classes-1.
    """
    spec = DATASETS[name]
    path = _fetch(spec["filename"], spec["url"])

    df = pd.read_csv(path, header=None, dtype=str, na_values=MISSING_MARKERS)
    num = df.apply(lambda col: pd.to_numeric(col, errors="coerce"))
    # A '?'-style marker that survived na_values would coerce to NaN anyway.
    tcol = spec["target_col"]
    feat_cols = [c for c in num.columns if c != tcol]

    X = num[feat_cols].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    y_raw = num[tcol].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    assert not np.isnan(y_raw).any(), f"unparsable labels in {name}"
    y = np.array([spec["class_map"][int(v)] for v in y_raw], dtype=int)

    meta = {
        "name": name,
        "source_url": spec["url"],
        "cached_path": path,
        "n_samples": int(X.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_classes": int(len(np.unique(y))),
        "class_counts": {int(c): int((y == c).sum()) for c in np.unique(y)},
        "n_missing_entries": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "missing_pct": float(100.0 * np.isnan(X).mean()),
        "per_feature_missing": {
            int(j): int(np.isnan(X[:, j]).sum()) for j in range(X.shape[1])
        },
        "note": spec["note"],
    }

    # Guard against silently loading the wrong file (paper Table 2 statistics).
    assert X.shape == (spec["n_samples"], spec["n_features"]), (
        f"{name}: expected shape {(spec['n_samples'], spec['n_features'])}, got {X.shape}"
    )
    assert meta["n_classes"] == spec["n_classes"], (
        f"{name}: expected {spec['n_classes']} classes, got {meta['n_classes']}"
    )
    return X, y, meta


if __name__ == "__main__":
    X, y, meta = load_dataset("hepatitis")
    for k, v in meta.items():
        if k != "per_feature_missing":
            print(f"{k}: {v}")
    print("per_feature_missing:", meta["per_feature_missing"])

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data — reimplementation from the paper
"Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data"
(arXiv:2510.13352), Section 4.

Implements exactly:
  Eq. (4)   equal-frequency bin centers c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)),
            k = 1..nbins  ->  centers include the min (0th pct) and max (100th pct)
            of the observed values of feature j.  [NB: this follows the paper's
            Eq. (4) literally; it supersedes the plan's provisional A13 guess of
            percentiles 100*k/(nbins+1).]
  Eq. (5)   proximity assignment b_{i,j} = argmin_k |x_{i,j} - c_{j,k}|
            (ties broken to the lowest bin index, assumption A3).
  Eq. (6-7) one-hot encoding h_{i,j} in {0,1}^nbins of the assigned bin for
            observed features, concatenated across features into z_i.
  Eq. (8-9) C_{i,j} = {m != i : b_{m,j} = b_{i,j}} (m implicitly has feature j
            observed, since b_{m,j} only exists then); S1(i) = intersection of
            C_{i,j} over observed features j of sample i.
  Eq. (10)  Level 1: h_{i,j} = mean of h_{m,j} over matching samples m.
            Assumption A8: the average is restricted to matching samples m with
            feature j observed (their h_{m,j} is a well-defined one-hot), so the
            estimator is single-pass and order-independent.
  Eq. (11-12) Level 2: S2(i) = union of C_{i,j}; same restricted mean.
  Eq. (13-14) Level 3: global prior p_{j,k} = (# samples in bin k of feature j)
            / (# samples with feature j observed); uniform 1/nbins if feature j
            has no observed values (assumption A7).
  Eq. (15-16) kernel K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n, i.e. K = (1/d) Z Z^T.

The representation Z (Eq. 7) is what the paper's K-means uses (Eq. 19); the
kernel matrix is provided for validation and kernel-method use.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def bin_centers(obs: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (4): evenly-spaced percentiles (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) of observed values."""
    if nbins < 2:  # degenerate; not part of the paper's grid {2,3,4,6,8}
        return np.array([np.median(obs)])
    pcts = (np.arange(nbins, dtype=float) * 100.0) / (nbins - 1.0)
    # linear interpolation between order statistics (assumption A2)
    return np.percentile(obs, pcts)


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int):
    """Bin centers (Eq. 4) and global bin priors (Eq. 13) per feature.

    Returns (centers, priors) where centers[j] is None for an entirely-missing
    feature (uniform prior 1/nbins is used instead, assumption A7).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    centers: list = []
    priors: list = []
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            priors.append(np.full(nbins, 1.0 / nbins, dtype=float))
            continue
        c = bin_centers(obs, nbins)
        centers.append(c)
        b = np.argmin(np.abs(obs[:, None] - c[None, :]), axis=1)  # ties -> lowest k
        counts = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors.append(counts / counts.sum())
    return centers, priors


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: list) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (5): proximity assignment. Returns B (n, d) int, -1 where missing."""
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        c = centers[j]
        if c is None:
            continue
        idx = np.where(~np.isnan(X[:, j]))[0]
        dist = np.abs(X[idx, j][:, None] - c[None, :])
        B[idx, j] = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)  # np.argmin ties -> lowest bin index
    return B


def build_representation(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int, return_H: bool = False):
    """Build the kernel representation Z (Eq. 7) with the cascading fallback
    (Sec. 4.2) for missing entries.

    Returns Z (n, d*nbins) plus a diagnostics dict (and H (n, d, nbins) if
    return_H is True).  Every per-feature encoding h_{i,j} sums to 1.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    n, d = X.shape
    observed = ~np.isnan(X)
    centers, priors = fit_bins(X, nbins)

    B = assign_bins(X, centers)
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        idx = np.where(observed[:, j])[0]
        H[idx, j, B[idx, j]] = 1.0  # Eq. (6)

            S2 = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)  # Eq. (11) union

"""Clustering evaluation: K-means on the proximity-kernel representation Z
(paper Sec. 5.1: "we applied K-means with the number of clusters to the
ground-truth number of classes"; Sec. 4.4 Eq. 19: k-means on z_i) and NMI.

Each experiment is run 10 times (R11) with different random seeds (A4) and
results are averaged.  nbins is searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8} (R12) and the
per-dataset value with the best 10-run average NMI is selected (A9).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score


def kmeans_nmi(
    Z: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    n_clusters: int,
    seed: int,
    n_init: int = 10,
) -> float:
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=seed)
    labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
    # sklearn default average_method='arithmetic' (assumption A5)
    return float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels))


def evaluate(
    Z: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    n_clusters: int,
    seeds: list[int],
    n_init: int = 10,
) -> dict:
    vals = [kmeans_nmi(Z, y, n_clusters, s, n_init=n_init) for s in seeds]
    return {
        "mean": float(np.mean(vals)),
        "std": float(np.std(vals)),
        "min": float(np.min(vals)),
        "max": float(np.max(vals)),
        "per_seed": vals,
        "seeds": list(seeds),
        "n_init": int(n_init),
    }


def search_nbins(
    X: np.ndarray,
    y: np.ndarray,
    n_clusters: int,
    nbins_grid: list[int],
    seeds: list[int],
    n_init: int = 10,
    build_fn=None,
) -> dict:
    """Search nbins over the grid (R12); select the best 10-run mean NMI (A9)."""
    if build_fn is None:
        from proximity_kernel import build_representation

        build_fn = build_representation

    results = []
    for nbins in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_fn(X, nbins)
        ev = evaluate(Z, y, n_clusters, seeds, n_init=n_init)
        results.append({"nbins": int(nbins), "nmi": ev, "diagnostics": diag})

    best = max(results, key=lambda r: r["nmi"]["mean"])  # ties -> first (lowest nbins)
    return {
        "best_nbins": int(best["nbins"]),
        "best": best,
        "all": results,
    }


def baseline_median_imputed(
    X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, n_clusters: int, seeds: list[int], n_init: int = 10
) -> dict:
    """Sanity diagnostic (not a paper claim): median imputation + standardization
    + K-means, to confirm the proximity-kernel result is not a trivial artifact."""
    from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
    from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

    Xi = SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit_transform(X)
    Xi = StandardScaler().fit_transform(Xi)
    return evaluate(Xi, y, n_clusters, seeds, n_init=n_init)

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Reproduce claim C1 of "Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for
Incomplete Data" (arXiv:2510.13352): NMI of the proposed proximity kernel on
the UCI Hepatitis dataset with K-means and the ground-truth number of clusters.

Protocol (paper Sec. 5.1 + claim contract):
  * equal-frequency bin centers by evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values
    (Eq. 4), proximity assignment to the nearest center (Eq. 5), one-hot
    encoding (Eq. 6-7), three-level cascading fallback for missing values
    (Sec. 4.2), kernel K = (1/d) Z Z^T (Eq. 15-16);
  * K-means on the representation Z (Eq. 19) with K = ground-truth number of
    classes, NMI as metric, 10 runs averaged (R10, R11);
  * nbins searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8} (R12), best 10-run mean NMI per
    dataset reported (A9).

Usage:
  python reproduce.py             # full reproduction (writes results/metrics.json)
  python reproduce.py --smoke     # 20-row smoke test with nbins=2 (no file writes)
  python reproduce.py --diagnose  # dataset/representation diagnostics only
  python reproduce.py --sensitivity  # documented protocol variants (no file writes)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SRC = os.path.join(HERE, "src")
if SRC not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SRC)

import cluster as cl  # noqa: E402
import data as data_mod  # noqa: E402
import proximity_kernel as pk  # noqa: E402

DATASET = "hepatitis"  # claim C1 dataset (Table 2 row "Hepatitis")
NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]  # paper Sec. 5.1 hyperparameter grid (R12)
SEEDS = list(range(10))  # R11 "conducted 10 times" (A4)
N_INIT = 10  # sklearn KMeans restarts (A4)
RESULTS_PATH = os.path.join(HERE, "results", "metrics.json")


def kernel_checks(Z: np.ndarray, d: int) -> dict:
    K = pk.proximity_kernel(Z, d)
    return {
        "symmetric": bool(np.allclose(K, K.T)),
        "min": float(K.min()),
        "max": float(K.max()),
        "max_diagonal": float(K.diagonal().max()),
        "min_diagonal": float(K.diagonal().min()),
        "in_unit_interval": bool(K.min() >= -1e-12 and K.max() <= 1 + 1e-12),
        "shape": [int(K.shape[0]), int(K.shape[1])],
    }


def encoding_checks(H: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    sums = H.sum(axis=2)
    return {
        "min_row_sum": float(sums.min()),
        "max_row_sum": float(sums.max()),
        "all_sum_to_one": bool(np.allclose(sums, 1.0)),
        "max_entry": float(H.max()),
        "min_entry": float(H.min()),
    }


def run_smoke(subset: int = 20, nbins: int = 2, seed: int = 0) -> None:
    """Smoke test on the first `subset` rows with a single nbins value."""
    X, y, meta = data_mod.load_dataset(DATASET)
    Xs, ys = X[:subset].copy(), y[:subset].copy()
    d = Xs.shape[1]
    n_classes = int(len(np.unique(ys)))
    print(f"[smoke] dataset {DATASET}: X{X.shape} -> subset X{Xs.shape}, classes={sorted(set(ys.tolist()))}")

    Z, diag, H = pk.build_representation(Xs, nbins, return_H=True)
    print(f"[smoke] Z shape: {Z.shape} (expected ({subset}, {d * nbins}))")
    assert Z.shape == (subset, d * nbins), f"bad Z shape {Z.shape}"
    assert np.isfinite(Z).all(), "Z contains NaN/inf"

    enc = encoding_checks(H)
    print(f"[smoke] encoding checks: {enc}")
    assert enc["all_sum_to_one"], "per-feature encodings must sum to 1"

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data — reimplementation from the paper
"Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data"
(arXiv:2510.13352), Section 4.

Implements exactly:
  Eq. (4)   equal-frequency bin centers c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)),
            k = 1..nbins  ->  centers include the min (0th pct) and max (100th pct)
            of the observed values of feature j.  [NB: this follows the paper's
            Eq. (4) literally; it supersedes the plan's provisional A13 guess of
            percentiles 100*k/(nbins+1), which is kept only as a sensitivity
            variant.]
  Eq. (5)   proximity assignment b_{i,j} = argmin_k |x_{i,j} - c_{j,k}|
            (ties broken to the lowest bin index, assumption A3).
  Eq. (6-7) one-hot encoding h_{i,j} in {0,1}^nbins of the assigned bin for
            observed features, concatenated across features into z_i.
  Eq. (8-9) C_{i,j} = {m != i : b_{m,j} = b_{i,j}} (m implicitly has feature j
            observed, since b_{m,j} only exists then); S1(i) = intersection of
            C_{i,j} over observed features j of sample i.
  Eq. (10)  Level 1: h_{i,j} = mean of h_{m,j} over matching samples m.
            Assumption A8 (primary): the average is restricted to matching
            samples m with feature j observed (their h_{m,j} is a well-defined
            one-hot), so the estimator is single-pass and order-independent.
            The literal reading of Eq. (10)/(12) — average over ALL of
            S1(i)/S2(i), with matching samples m that are themselves missing
            feature j contributing that feature's global prior p_j — is
            implemented in build_representation_literal and used only as a
            sensitivity variant.
  Eq. (11-12) Level 2: S2(i) = union of C_{i,j}; same restricted mean.
  Eq. (13-14) Level 3: global prior p_{j,k} = (# samples in bin k of feature j)
            / (# samples with feature j observed); uniform 1/nbins if feature j
            has no observed values (assumption A7).
  Eq. (15-16) kernel K(x_m, x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n, i.e. K = (1/d) Z Z^T.

The representation Z (Eq. 7) is what the paper's K-means uses (Eq. 19); the
kernel matrix is provided for validation and kernel-method use.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def bin_centers(obs: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (4): evenly-spaced percentiles (k-1)*100/(nbins-1) of observed values."""
    if nbins < 2:  # degenerate; not part of the paper's grid {2,3,4,6,8}
        return np.array([np.median(obs)])
    pcts = (np.arange(nbins, dtype=float) * 100.0) / (nbins - 1.0)
    # linear interpolation between order statistics (assumption A2)
    return np.percentile(obs, pcts)


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int):
    """Bin centers (Eq. 4) and global bin priors (Eq. 13) per feature.

    Returns (centers, priors) where centers[j] is None for an entirely-missing
    feature (uniform prior 1/nbins is used instead, assumption A7).
    """
    d = X.shape[1]
    centers: list = []
    priors: list = []
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)
            priors.append(np.full(nbins, 1.0 / nbins, dtype=float))
            continue
        c = bin_centers(obs, nbins)
        centers.append(c)
        b = np.argmin(np.abs(obs[:, None] - c[None, :]), axis=1)  # ties -> lowest k
        counts = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        priors.append(counts / counts.sum())
    return centers, priors


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: list) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (5): proximity assignment. Returns B (n, d) int, -1 where missing."""
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        c = centers[j]
        if c is None:
            continue
        idx = np.where(~np.isnan(X[:, j]))[0]
        dist = np.abs(X[idx, j][:, None] - c[None, :])
        B[idx, j] = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)  # np.argmin ties -> lowest bin index
    return B


def build_representation(
    X: np.ndarray,
    nbins: int,
    return_H: bool = False,
    centers: list | None = None,
    priors: list | None = None,
    literal: bool = False,
):
    """Build the kernel representation Z (Eq. 7) with the cascading fallback
    (Sec. 4.2) for missing entries.

    literal=False (primary, A8): for a missing entry (i, j) the mean is taken
    over matching samples m that have feature j observed.
    literal=True (sensitivity variant): the mean is taken over all of
    S1(i)/S2(i) exactly as written in Eq. (10)/(12); a matching sample m that
    is itself missing feature j contributes that feature's global prior p_j.

    Returns Z (n, d*nbins) plus a diagnostics dict (and H (n, d, nbins) if
    return_H is True).  Every per-feature encoding h_{i,j} sums to 1.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
    n, d = X.shape
    observed = ~np.isnan(X)
    if centers is None or priors is None:
        centers, priors = fit_bins(X, nbins)

    B = assign_bins(X, centers)
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        idx = np.where(observed[:, j])[0]
        H[idx, j, B[idx, j]] = 1.0  # Eq. (6)

    if literal:
        # encoding usable in Eq. (10)/(12) sums: one-hot if observed else prior p_j
        H_avail = H.copy()
        for j in range(d):
            H_avail[~observed[:, j], j] = priors[j]

    level_counts = {1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0}
    n_samples_with_missing = 0
    for i in range(n):
        mis = np.where(~observed[i])[0]
        if mis.size == 0:
            continue
        n_samples_with_missing += 1
        obs_feats = np.where(observed[i])[0]
        if obs_feats.size:
            S1 = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)  # Eq. (9) intersection
            S2 = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)  # Eq. (11) union
            for l in obs_feats:
                m = (B[:, l] == B[i, l]) & observed[:, l]  # Eq. (8)
                m[i] = False  # "m != i"

proximity_kernel returns (Z@Z.T)/d; clean run checks symmetry, [0,1] range, unit diagonal. Clustering uses Z, which is equivalent to kernel k-means on (1/d)ZZ^T up to a global distance scale.
cluster.kmeans_nmi uses sklearn KMeans with n_clusters=ground-truth K=2 and sklearn normalized_mutual_info_score; full transductive dataset per A10.
SEEDS=range(10), run_full averages 10 per-seed NMIs; metrics.json records per_seed length 10 for each nbins. For nbins=2 the per-seed values are identical (std 0.0).
NBINS_GRID=[2,3,4,6,8]; search_nbins evaluates all five and selects best 10-run mean (A9); metrics.json per_nbins has all five.

No scaling benchmark or linearity check is included. The fallback implementation loops over all n samples for each missing sample/observed feature (worst-case O(d n^2) for the boolean intersections), so the paper's O(nd+d n log n) complexity is not demonstrated by this code, although the n=155 clean run finishes in 2.8 s.

For a complete row, every observed entry sets exactly one bin per feature, so H has exactly d ones out of d*nbins; for incomplete rows observed features remain sparse one-hot and only missing entries receive fractional vectors.
